patients.summary: Elementary school teacher with long-standing type 1 diabetes and Hashimoto hypothyroidism who joins in 2022. Alopecia areata is diagnosed by dermatology in 2024, she is admitted with DKA during a viral URI in February 2025, and in October 2025 she has idiopathic acute transverse myelitis with a good recovery through rehab and PT.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, new patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
31 y/o woman, elementary school teacher, transferring care from her prior primary care office; wanted a practice where she can reach the doctor directly. Records requested.

Type 1 diabetes, long-standing. On Lantus 18 units at bedtime and Humalog with meals, counting carbs at 1 unit per 12 g with a correction scale. Checks fingersticks 4-5 times a day. No severe lows, no ED visits for sugars that she can recall. Last eye exam about a year ago, told no retinopathy.

Hashimoto hypothyroidism on levothyroxine 88 mcg, takes it first thing with water. Feels well on it.

PMH: as above. PSH: wisdom teeth out at 18.
Meds: insulin glargine 18 u qHS; insulin lispro per carb ratio 1:12 + correction; levothyroxine 88 mcg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
FH: mother Hashimoto's. Father type 2 DM. Maternal aunt with RA. Sister has celiac disease.
SH: lives in Amherst with a roommate. Teaches 2nd grade. Never smoked. A drink once or twice a month. No drugs. Walks most evenings.

ROS: negative except as above. No polyuria, no numbness in the feet, no vision change.

Exam: vitals as charted. Well appearing. HEENT unremarkable, thyroid smooth, not enlarged, no nodules. No adenopathy. Heart regular rate and rhythm, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, no tenderness; injection sites in the abdomen without lipohypertrophy. Extremities no edema. Feet: skin intact, pulses 2+ DP/PT, monofilament sensation intact bilaterally. Scalp and skin normal.

PHQ-2 0.

A/P
1. Type 1 diabetes: A1c, CMP, urine albumin/creatinine, lipids today. Continue current regimen. Eye exam due — she will book with her optometrist.
2. Hashimoto hypothyroidism: TSH today, continue 88 mcg.
3. Health maintenance: flu shot this fall at a nurse visit. Prior office records for Pap and vaccine history.
Return in 3 months for diabetes follow-up.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Christine, your labs from Wednesday are in. A1c is 7.1, close to where your prior office had you. Thyroid level is normal on the 88 mcg, kidney function and urine protein are normal, cholesterol is good, blood counts are normal. No changes. See you in November.

documents.title: Records from prior primary care office
documents.author: MA
documents.body:
Outside records received (38 pages) and scanned to media.

Abstracted for the chart:
- Problems: type 1 diabetes mellitus; Hashimoto hypothyroidism.
- Medications: insulin glargine 18 units at bedtime; insulin lispro with meals by carb ratio; levothyroxine 88 mcg daily.
- Allergies: NKDA.
- Cervical cytology 2021: negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy.
- Immunizations: childhood series complete including hepatitis B x3 and MMR x2. Last Td/Tdap date not documented.
- A1c values over the past two years in the 7s.

Forwarded to PCP for review.

documents.title: Refill request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy fax requesting levothyroxine 88 mcg, now under our office. Last TSH 8/17 normal. Sent 90-day supply with 3 refills per PCP.

documents.title: Nurse Visit — Influenza Vaccine
documents.author: RN
documents.body: In after school for flu vaccine. No fever today, no prior reactions. Influenza quadrivalent 0.5 mL IM left deltoid. VIS provided. Waited 15 min, no issues.

documents.title: COVID booster
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hello — just letting you know I got the new bivalent COVID booster at the pharmacy on Saturday (Pfizer). Sore arm and a little tired Sunday, fine now.

documents.title: RE: COVID booster
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Thanks Christine, I've added it to your immunization record.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Diabetes Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: 3-month DM f/u. Busy start to the school year; snacking more in the afternoons and not always bolusing for it. Fasting sugars 120s-150s on her meter log. One low to 58 after a long walk, treated with juice. No numbness or vision change.
Meds: glargine 18 u qHS, lispro 1:12 + correction, levothyroxine 88 mcg.

O: vitals as charted. Alert, well. Heart regular, lungs clear. Injection sites ok.

A/P: T1DM. A1c today. Talked about pre-bolusing for the afternoon snack or picking low-carb options. Keep glargine at 18 for now — fastings are acceptable. Reviewed treating lows, carrying glucose tabs on walks. F/u 3 months.

documents.title: A1c result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: A1c came back 7.4 — a touch up from August, which fits the afternoon snacks we talked about. Nothing to change in your doses. Let's recheck in February.

documents.title: Prior authorization — insulin pens
documents.author: MA
documents.body: New plan year. Pharmacy says Humalog KwikPen needs PA renewal. Submitted with T1DM diagnosis and current regimen. Approved through 12/31/2023. Pharmacy notified, pt notified via portal.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Diabetes Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Doing better with the afternoon snack — switched to cheese and nuts on school days. Meter average down a bit. No lows below 60 since November. Fasting 110s-140s.

Exam: BP and weight as charted. Well appearing. No lipohypertrophy.

T1DM — A1c today. No dose changes. Hypothyroid — stable, TSH due in August. Reminded about the eye exam; she has an appointment next month. Back in 3 months.

documents.title: Diabetic eye examination report
documents.author: optometry
documents.body:
Diabetic eye examination
Date of exam: 03/14/2023
Patient: Christine Hartley

History: type 1 diabetes. No visual complaints.
Visual acuity corrected 20/20 OD and OS. IOP normal OU. Anterior segment normal.
Dilated fundus exam: no diabetic retinopathy OU. No macular edema. Discs healthy.

Impression: type 1 diabetes without retinopathy.
Recommendation: repeat dilated exam in 12 months.

Thank you for allowing us to participate in her care.

documents.title: Appointment cancelled
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Pt called to cancel tomorrow's 3:45 — end-of-year school events. Rebooked as a video visit 6/7 with labs beforehand. Lab order already in.

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Video Visit — Diabetes
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video, patient at home, identity verified, consented to video care.

A1c 7.4 from 6/2. She thinks the last few weeks of school were chaotic — lunch on the run, some missed lunch boluses that she corrected for later. Summer is coming and she does better with routine. No lows needing help. No new symptoms.

Plan: no change in doses. Physical in August with yearly labs. Message us with any meter patterns over the summer.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam before school starts. Good summer — hiking, sleeping well, sugars steadier. No lows needing assistance.

Meds: glargine 18 u qHS; lispro 1:12 + correction; levothyroxine 88 mcg daily. NKDA.
FH unchanged (mother Hashimoto's, father T2DM, maternal aunt RA, sister celiac).
SH: teaching 2nd grade again this fall. Never smoker, 1-2 drinks a month.

ROS: negative for chest pain, dyspnea, GI symptoms, numbness, weight change, hair or skin change.

Exam: vitals as charted. General well. Eyes, ears, oropharynx normal. Neck supple; thyroid normal size, no nodules. Heart RRR without murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. Skin clear. Neuro grossly normal. Diabetic foot exam: skin intact, no calluses, DP/PT 2+, monofilament intact 10/10 sites bilaterally.

PHQ-2: 0.

Assessment/Plan
- T1DM: A1c, CMP, lipids, urine albumin/creatinine. Continue regimen.
- Hashimoto: TSH.
- Celiac screen given T1DM and her sister's celiac: tTG-IgA today.
- One-time HIV and hepatitis C screening — she agrees.
- Tdap today (last date unknown). PCV20 today given diabetes.
- Pap: last 2021 normal, due 2024.
- Flu shot in October.
RTC 3 months.

documents.title: Physical labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Christine — all good news from Wednesday. A1c 6.8, your best since joining us. Thyroid normal, kidneys and urine protein normal, cholesterol fine. The celiac antibody screen is negative. HIV and hepatitis C screens are negative. Enjoy the last week of summer.

documents.title: Nurse Visit — Influenza Vaccine
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu vaccine. Feeling well, afebrile. Influenza quadrivalent 0.5 mL IM right deltoid, lot recorded. VIS given. No reaction after 15 minutes.

documents.title: Updated COVID shot
documents.author: patient
documents.body: FYI I had the updated COVID vaccine at the pharmacy this past Saturday. No problems.

documents.title: RE: Updated COVID shot
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Recorded — thank you!

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Diabetes Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
DM f/u. Halloween and parent conferences — more grazing, a few post-dinner readings over 250. Fastings still 120s-140s. No lows. Feels fine.

Vitals as charted. Exam unremarkable; sites ok.

T1DM: A1c today. Talked through bolusing for grazing (smaller boluses, or a set snack). Holiday season ahead — she knows the drill. No dose changes. RTC late Feb, video is fine.

documents.title: Humalog refill
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, I'm down to my last box of Humalog pens and the pharmacy says I'm out of refills. Could you send a new prescription before the break? Thanks!

documents.title: RE: Humalog refill
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Sent — same dosing, a year of refills. Your A1c from November was 7.6, a little higher with the season; nothing to change. Happy holidays.
